claims.text: The baseline Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr-containing refractory HEA has moderate high-temperature strength.
The baseline refractory HEA has good room-temperature ductility.
Adding 0.5–1.0 wt% yttrium will cause in situ formation of Y2O3 nanoprecipitates.
The resulting Y2O3 particles will be ultrafine and uniformly dispersed in the alloy matrix.
Dispersed oxide or carbide reinforcement particles can strengthen an HEA matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will stabilize or pin grain boundaries in the proposed refractory HEA.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will inhibit dislocation motion in the proposed refractory HEA.
Particle reinforcement can produce a substantial mechanical-strength increase relative to an unreinforced HEA baseline.
The yttrium-modified alloy will improve high-temperature yield strength by at least 20% relative to the yttrium-free baseline at approximately 950°C.
The yttrium-modified alloy will improve creep resistance by at least 20% relative to the yttrium-free baseline at approximately 950°C.
The 0.5–1.0 wt% yttrium addition will preserve room-temperature ductility.
The 0.5–1.0 wt% yttrium addition will cause negligible change in material density.
Restricting yttrium to 0.5–1.0 wt% will avoid formation of deleterious phases that impair room-temperature properties.
The Y2O3 dispersion may be unstable or nonuniform during prolonged high-temperature exposure.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis uses 'at least a 20%' improvement, the predicted outcome says 'exceeding 20%,' and the falsification rule accepts an improvement of exactly 20%; the treatment of the boundary value is inconsistent.
